title: Install surge coordination & open asks — week of Aug 10
content:
Summary:
Week of Aug 10 — coordinating an install surge across three medium-to-large customers. Focus areas: network handoffs, GPU driver reconciliation, and KMS onboarding. This note is for internal alignment: field teams, SRE, infra, and solutions engineering.

High-level status (snapshot):
- 6 active installs in flight (3 critical, 2 progressing, 1 warm standby).
- Two installs at risk of missing SLA due to network preflight failures and delayed customer NOC approvals.
- Short-term mitigation: rolling red-team of two engineers to unblock DNS/MTU and driver issues (see action items).

Quick wins delivered this week:
- KV cache warmup script deployed to edge sites (reduces first-request latency on warmup by ~30%). Marco authored an idempotent wrapper to avoid duplicate warmups.
- Ansible playbook patched to make kubelet restart logic safe for multi-node clusters (avoids systemd race we saw last month).
- Basic KMS smoke harness added to onboarding checklists (Leah).

Active installs (customer-level notes):
1) HelixHealth — "greenfield" VPC + on-prem sync
   - Status: at-risk
   - Blocker: customer firewall team applied a 1500->1400 MTU change without telling our install lead; caused jumbo frame mismatch between NICs and site routers (packet fragmentation + gRPC stalls).
   - Mitigation: suggested temporary MTU clamp to 1400 on agent level; SRE to validate since this increases packet count for high-throughput inference. Diego and Priya coordinating with customer NOC; expecting approval by 8/14.
   - Next step: if customer doesn't approve, schedule a night window to change MTU across affected hosts (owner: Diego, ETA: 8/15 02:00-04:00).

2) NimbleDocs — dedicated VPC w/ private deploy (onprem DB integration)
   - Status: progressing
   - Blocker: OEM GPU driver (NVIDIA 540) incompatible with our nvfuser kernel for quantized runtime on the 4090s they provided. Fallback to CPU would breach latency SLOs.
   - Mitigation path: request customer allow us to install vendor-certified 545.x driver (security review required). Priya submitted the driver change request (JIRA-8599). Temporary: enable mixed-precision path for smaller batches to keep p95 within 1.8x of target.
   - Action: Solutions Eng runbook update to include explicit driver-version gating and required vendor ints (owner: Priya, ETA: 8/16).

3) Orpheus Labs — VPC-only, high-throughput batch workloads
   - Status: blocked -> infra capacity limit for Dedicated pool
   - Blocker: autoscaling policy misconfigured (min nodes set too low, burst disabled). Result: identical requests queued and timed out during load test.
   - Mitigation: temporary override to increase min nodes + enable burst for 24h while ops team does a capacity bump. Ops request created (JIRA-8523).
   - Notes: Need a postmortem for rollout policy tests — SRE to lead.

Cross-cutting issues we keep seeing:
- DNS TTL variation between customer environments and our edge-proxy caching causes cache invalidation storms on route changes. We need a standard guidance document and possibly a small TTL-mapper utility.
- Handshake flakiness when KMS integration is in the middle of customer key rotation: observed ~1.5% decrypt failure rate during rotation windows; recovery was automatic but caused ~5m of elevated erroring for one customer.
- Sparse telemetry on on-prem switches (SNMP rate limits and ACLs often block our probes). Recommend adding a minimal passive-checklist that avoids SNMP where customers have strict policies.

Telemetry snapshot (rolling 48h):
- Median token latency across active installs: 72ms
- p95 token latency: 410ms (spike correlated with Orpheus load test on 8/11)
- Failed job rate (install scripts): 4.2% -> major contributors MTU mismatches (HelixHealth) and driver checks (NimbleDocs).

Oncall / Field staffing notes:
- Field rotation this week: Marco (primary), Leah (secondary), Diego (weekend oncall). Add note: Marco needs a backup for 8/14 (scheduled PTO) — Priya to cover if available.
- Tools requested by field: lightweight network-check binary that runs common checks without root (customer legal often denies root-level scripts). Marco prototyped net-check v0.1 (link in linked_artifacts).

Open asks (action required cross-team):
- Security: expedited review for driver 545.x for NimbleDocs (owner: security, contact: Maya R.). Ticket: JIRA-8599.
- SRE: approve temporary MTU clamp on dedicated pools and document cost implications (owner: SRE ops lead).
- Product/Console: add a small flag in rollout UI to allow "burst override" for Dedicated pools to support emergency scale-ups (owner: Product-Console; business impact noted by Orpheus case).
- Solutions Eng: create a short "preflight NOC checklist" one-pager to be handed to customers before installs (owner: Leah; ETA: 8/18).

Risks & dependencies:
- Risk: if HelixHealth network remains misaligned we may need 4-6 engineer-hours during a night window to coordinate routers + host MTU changes — impacts resources for other installs.
- Dependency: KMS team needs to provide a deterministically testable key-rotation simulator (low effort, high value for our onboarding checks).

Action items (owner / due / status):
- Diego: Schedule night MTU maintenance for HelixHealth (due 2026-08-15 02:00, status: waiting on NOC approval).
- Priya: Driver change request & security follow-up for NimbleDocs (due 2026-08-16, status: in_progress, JIRA-8599).
- Marco: Finish net-check v0.1, drop binary + README to deploy-scripts (due 2026-08-13, status: done; PR link in linked_artifacts).
- Leah: Preflight NOC checklist + KMS smoke steps one-pager (due 2026-08-18, status: in_progress).
- SRE Ops Lead: Approve temporary dedicated-pool burst override (due 2026-08-14, status: requested, JIRA-8523).

Notes for next sync:
- Bring a short demo of net-check and the KV warmup script to the Monday field sync (5–10 min).
- Proposal: add an "install readiness" flag in the console showing a consolidated green/yellow/red status for: network preflight, driver check, KMS connection, and node GPU compatibility. This would reduce back-and-forth with customer NOCs.

Appendix (raw evidence snippets):
- HelixHealth NIC trace: truncated packet fragments observed at 1:22am 2026-08-11 (attached to JIRA-8672).
- NimbleDocs driver test log: crash on cuDNN init when using 540.x driver (log: /var/log/install/nimble/driver-test-20260811.log).
- Orpheus load test report: burst queue lengths and scaling timestamps (see Confluence linked above).

If you are owning an action item and need help reassigning or adding time, ping #private-deploys and tag the person in the doc with a quick note.

— Avery
